Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 22.1 grants Vendor unlimited, unannounced audits of Customer plus remote access to our systems — squarely in the playbook walk-away zone. The rule requires no more than one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no direct access to Customer systems. Sections 22.2 (Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment; no direct system access) and 22.3 (findings confidential) already meet the playbook, and Section 23 contains no additional records-inspection rights, so the minimal fix is to rewrite 22.1 with the frequency, notice, scope and access limits.

Original paragraphs:
p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Rendered redline:
p0093: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer's operations. The audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor that is not a Customer competitor and that is bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as Section 16. The audit shall be limited to a review of records relevant to Customer's use of the Services, conducted remotely from the auditor's own facilities or at a mutually agreed location, and Vendor and its auditor shall have no direct or remote access to Customer's systems.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have limited audits to once per twelve months on thirty days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed the right of remote access to our systems, consistent with our playbook position that audits be rare, notified and off-site (records review only). Cost allocation in Section 22.2 is acceptable as drafted; if helpful we can accept fifteen days' notice as a fallback.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies the preferred position. 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 warrants each Deliverable for ninety days after the later of delivery or acceptance and warrants hosted Services conformity for the entire subscription term (better than the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality reduction and open-source protection. 19.4 supplies the required remedy ladder of re-performance, repair or replacement with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure, and expressly preserves other remedies. 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or other stated remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties. Acceptance mechanics in 6.1–6.2 (no deemed acceptance, correction cycles, refund on repeated failure) reinforce the warranty. No customer-adverse gap warrants an edit.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already delivers our preferred warranty package:

- **19.1** — professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **19.2** — 90 days for each Deliverable measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance, and hosted Services warranted to conform *throughout the subscription term* (this exceeds the 12-month software benchmark, so no extension is needed).
- **19.3** — compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **19.4** — the full remedy ladder (re-perform, repair, replace; termination plus refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period) and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement meets our preferred position: no minimum commitment, fees for ordered/usage services only. § 2.1 (p0012) expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms that declining to place further orders is not a breach or shortfall. § 7.1 (p0026) bars Vendor from imposing minimum-use or similar charges not identified in the Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0050) records that Customer has made no minimum-volume (or exclusivity/MFC) commitment. "Order Form" (§ 1.6) covers only quantities Customer actually signs for, so no take-or-pay is imported at the Order Form level, and no shortfall penalty, forecast obligation, or non-cancellable/prepaid-forfeiture language appears elsewhere (the only "shortfall" references, §§ 22.2–22.3, concern audit underpayments, not volume). Auto-renewal in § 8.2 extends term length rather than creating a purchase commitment and is addressed by the separate renewal rule. No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
p0026: 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.
p0050: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Affiliate: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies the preferred position. 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 warrants each Deliverable for ninety days after the later of delivery or acceptance and warrants hosted Services conformity for the entire subscription term (better than the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality reduction and open-source protection. 19.4 supplies the required remedy ladder of re-performance, repair or replacement with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure, and expressly preserves other remedies. 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or other stated remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties. Acceptance mechanics in 6.1–6.2 (no deemed acceptance, correction cycles, refund on repeated failure) reinforce the warranty. No customer-adverse gap warrants an edit.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already delivers our preferred warranty package:

- **19.1** — professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **19.2** — 90 days for each Deliverable measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance, and hosted Services warranted to conform *throughout the subscription term* (this exceeds the 12-month software benchmark, so no extension is needed).
- **19.3** — compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **19.4** — the full remedy ladder (re-perform, repair, replace; termination plus refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period) and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The warranty package is otherwise strong: 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and no malicious code; 19.4 gives re-performance, repair or replacement with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; and 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties while preserving express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies. The one gap against our preferred position is duration: Deliverables (which include configurations, integrations and other software work product under the definition in 1.4) carry only a ninety-day conformance period, whereas our preferred position is twelve months for software, with ninety days reserved for services. Hosted Services are already warranted for the whole subscription term, so the fix is confined to the Deliverable period. Minimal redline extends 19.2 to twelve (12) months, stated numerically; fallback is an express ninety (90) days with the 19.4 remedy untouched.

Original paragraphs:
p0077: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
p0079: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
p0080: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

## Executive Summary

4. **Leverage the internal inconsistencies.** Sections 2.1 and 12.3 already record that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We should present §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 as conforming edits to the parties' stated bargain rather than as new asks.
5. **Confirm no further movement is sought** on the compliant provisions (§§ 11, 13, 14, 18, 20, 21, 24, 28 and 2.1) so that reciprocal Vendor requests in those areas can be resisted.
6. **Escalate** if Vendor declines to move on any of the four walk-away items, and report back to the deal team before further drafting."}
